questions.question: What creates objects before main() execution?
questions.explanation: Static constructors initialize static members.

questions.question: What ensures proper copy semantics?
questions.explanation: Rule of three covers destructor, copy constructor, assignment operator.

questions.question: What C++11 rule adds move operations?
questions.explanation: Rule of five includes move constructor and move assignment.

questions.question: What technique defers object initialization?
questions.explanation: Lazy initialization creates objects only when needed.

questions.question: What C++ feature guarantees exception safety?
questions.explanation: RAII ties resource lifetime to object lifetime.

questions.question: What pattern creates objects with many parameters?
questions.explanation: Builder pattern constructs complex objects step-by-step.

questions.question: What technique allocates objects in memory pools?
questions.explanation: Placement new constructs objects at specific addresses.

questions.question: What prevents default constructor generation?
questions.explanation: Defining any constructor suppresses default generation.

questions.question: What C++11 keyword delegates constructor work?
questions.explanation: Delegating constructors call other constructors.

questions.question: What manages object pools efficiently?
questions.explanation: Object pooling reuses objects instead of creating new ones.

questions.question: In Java, class A has A() calling this(5) and A(int x) printing x — what does new A() print?
questions.explanation: Constructor chaining with this(5) invokes A(int x) which prints 5.

questions.question: In C++, members are initialized in what order regardless of initializer-list order?
questions.explanation: Members initialize in the order they are declared, not listed.

questions.question: What C++11 syntax explicitly disables compiler-generated copy semantics?
questions.explanation: Marking functions = delete prevents their generation and use.

questions.question: What must Python's __new__ return for __init__ to execute?
questions.explanation: __init__ only runs if __new__ returns an instance of the class.

questions.question: What C++ guideline recommends declaring no special member functions at all?
questions.explanation: The rule of zero lets the compiler generate all special members.

questions.question: In Java, what is printed by `class A { { print("I"); } A() { print("C"); } } class B extends A { { print("i"); } B() { print("c"); } }` on `new B()`?
questions.explanation: Order: parent instance initializer, parent constructor, child instance initializer, child constructor.

questions.question: A Java constructor contains `super(); this(5);` — what is the result?
questions.explanation: this() must be the first statement; combining it with super() is illegal.

questions.question: The default C++ copy constructor copies a pointer member — what kind of copy results when you duplicate such an object?
questions.explanation: Only the pointer value is copied; both objects share the same pointee.

questions.question: In Python, what happens if `__init__` returns a non-None value such as `return self`?
questions.explanation: Python raises TypeError: __init__() should return None.

questions.question: You define `class C { C(int x) {} }` in Java and call `new C()` — what happens?
questions.explanation: Once any constructor is declared, no default constructor is generated, so new C() fails to compile.
